newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast 1996/97 cocoa exporters list out.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast 1996/97 cocoa exporters list out.

text.p: Exporters licenced by Ivory Coast for the 1996/97 cocoa and coffee season were notified on Saturday and a final government statement of guidelines on exporters' rates is due on Monday, exporters and trade sources said on Saturday.
Ivory Coast's 1996/97 cocoa marketing season was opened on October 24 but uncertainty over licencing, and buying and marketing rates, had slowed port arrivals and exports of cocoa.
The list, signed by the Minister of Commerce on Friday and agreed by Ivory Coast's Caisse de Stabilisation marketing board (Caistab), lists 41 approved exporters.
The full list, obtained by Reuters, includes the following exporters:
SIFCA CIPEXI DAFCI JAG COMIVOIRE
SOGIMEX CIC CIVEXIM SONEGI COMAFRIQUE
EL NASR SAIE SOIMEXY DELBAU SACO CHOCODI
UNICAO VICI SICC SIDAI INTERNEGOCE
PROCI BORRO SHAC SICAFCA CAPA
SICPA AFRECO PRN TROPIVAL MPC PACI
PACI SOCOP AFCOM EBURNEA IPN
SICPRO SEPRIV SOPRIVO AFROCOM CAFCAO
ERAF

Exporters had expected some to lose their licences after 1995/96 for not paying debts to the Caistab, failing to put up a deposit of 100 million CFA francs for 1996/97 or being unable to prove bank funds of 200 million CFA.
"There are more rather than less but the list is set. The Caisse seems to have given in on some," said an exporter.
Exporters said banks would renew buying finance for 1996/97 from Monday if the exporters rates are known by then.
"The Societe Generale de Banque was cutting credit because the central bank stopped refinance for banks lending to non-approved exporters," said one exporter.
Exporters and shipping lines expect a rush of November cocoa arrivals, which had slowed due to uncertainty over when the 1996/97 cocoa marketing season would get fully underway.
"Give it a week or so and we should get back into a normal rhythm. People will need a few days to tie up finance," said an exporter.
Ivory Coast's coffee marketing season starts late in December or early in January 1997. A final date and coffee marketing rates have not been set. --Abidjan Newsroom +225 21 21 90
